pages.title: Introduction to the module on Strings
pages.content:
So far, we have focused on logic, integers, math. \
The module on logic building and problem solving primarily covered number operations. 

It is time to add 'Strings' to our arsenal for solving programming problems.

Lets revise some basic syntax of strings.
- Strings are a **datatype**.
  - A string is composed of characters. A single character can be any letter, any digit, symbol, etc.
  - A **binary string** is one which has only '0' and '1' as component characters
  - The character in the $i^{th}$ index of a string is represented as **S[i]**

Click in **Next** to proceed.

pages.title: Review problem - 1
pages.content:
Malvika likes only $2$ colours - amber and brass. \
Her mother bought $n$ balloons - each of which is either amber or brass in colour. \
The colours of the balls is provided as a string consisting of characters 'a' and 'b'
- 'a' denotes amber coloured balloon
- 'b' denotes brass coloured balloon

Malvika wants all balloons to be of the same colour - she can paint some balloons with opposite colour. \
Find out the **minimum** number of balloons she needs to paint to make all of them the same colour.
